unmatched.quote: Score 10: exactly on the threshold. One more clue and it goes to junk; one fewer and it reaches the inbox.
unmatched.problem: The rule (b4.config.decision.threshold = 10, bh.rule 'score is 10 or more goes to junk') sends a score of exactly 10 to junk. The string says it takes one more clue to reach junk, but a score of 10 is already junk. The same text appears in hi ('एक सुराग और, तो यह जंक में जाएगा') and te ('ఇంకో ఆధారం ఉంటే జంక్‌కి వెళ్తుంది'). It also contradicts knob.sentence, which will print 'goes to junk' at 10.
unmatched.why: Check numbers-and-working: text must match the configured rule. It also teaches the wrong meaning of 'at or above', which is the core objective o1. A learner who reaches the goal is told something false at the moment of success.
unmatched.fix: Rewrite in all three locales, for example: 'Score 10: exactly on the threshold, and 10 is enough to go to junk. One point fewer and it reaches the inbox.'

unmatched.quote: Nobody sets their points by hand: the filter works them out from millions of messages that people marked as junk.
unmatched.problem: The absolute claim is false. Many real filters, such as rule-based systems with hand-tuned or hand-reviewed scores, still have people set or adjust points or rules, and modern filters combine learned and hand-written parts. Also, learned filters need examples marked as junk and as not junk. The same absolute wording is in hi ('कोई हाथ से तय नहीं करता') and te ('ఎవరూ చేత్తో పెట్టరు').
unmatched.why: Check factual-accuracy: a simplification that becomes false. It reinforces misconception 3 in the other direction and overstates what is known about 'real filters'.
unmatched.fix: Say: 'Many real filters do not have their points set by hand: the filter works them out from millions of example messages that people marked as junk or as real. That is called training.' Apply the same softening and the 'junk or real' addition to hi and te.

unmatched.quote: Write up to five messages that you think would fool this filter.
unmatched.problem: The block invites free-text input with no statement that what is typed stays on this device and no instruction to keep real personal details out. yd.e1 ('reply with your address') models a message that asks for an address, and the classroom variant (maxItems 12) may display learners' messages to the class. The same applies to hi and te.
unmatched.why: Check privacy and the learner-online-safety reference: inputs like 'your own messages' must say what you type stays on this device and must never invite anything that identifies a person (Article 10; docs/11). Nothing personal may appear on a shared classroom screen.
unmatched.fix: Add to yd.prompt in all locales: 'Make up your messages. Do not use real names, phone numbers, addresses or school names. What you type stays on this device.' In classroom mode, show only counts or teacher-approved examples, not learner text.

unmatched.quote: work out its score with the points above
unmatched.problem: The instruction depends on the position of earlier content. b13 is separated from the point values in b4 by many blocks, and in a linear or screen-reader reading, or after a detour, 'above' does not point to anything clear. The point values are not restated. Hindi ('ऊपर के अंकों से') and Telugu ('పై పాయింట్లతో') do the same.
unmatched.why: Check accessibility-content: instructions must name things in words and must not rely on position. It also breaks Article 6 (every step of a calculation is shown).
unmatched.fix: Restate the rule in the prompt: 'work out its score: 1 point for each “!”, 2 for each money word, 3 for each urgent word. Would it reach 10?' Do the same in hi and te.

unmatched.quote: क्रिकेट अभ्यास शुक्रवार को हो गया है
unmatched.problem: English says 'Football practice moved to Friday', a schedule change. The Hindi means 'Cricket practice has happened on Friday', which is a past event, and drops 'moved'. Switching football to cricket is an acceptable locale variant. The meaning change is not.
unmatched.why: Check locale-fidelity: nothing dropped or changed in meaning. A learner may read the message differently, and bh.i6 says it is a real, clue-free message.
unmatched.fix: Use 'क्रिकेट अभ्यास शुक्रवार को कर दिया गया है' or, more clearly, 'क्रिकेट अभ्यास अब शुक्रवार को होगा'.

unmatched.quote: एक संदेश में लिखा है “मीटिंग 3 बजे हो गई है।”
unmatched.problem: English quotes 'Meeting moved to 3 pm.' The Hindi says the meeting has already happened at 3 and drops the idea of moving. Telugu ('మీటింగ్ మధ్యాహ్నం 3కి మారింది') keeps the meaning.
unmatched.why: Check locale-fidelity: the quoted message is a learning artifact and must say the same thing in each locale.
unmatched.fix: Use “मीटिंग अब 3 बजे होगी।” or “मीटिंग 3 बजे कर दी गई है।”
